provenance: PR #52 review round 1, findings R4 and R5. Both are the same defect in two shapes: a held-out case's provenance stated a byte-level fact the committed fixture does not support — c-2025 claimed a case-insensitive item-plus-digit regex 'returns exactly four hits' without naming the regex (the regex that fits the three offsets it then lists returns THREE, and the named fourth entry contains no digit at all), and intc-2025 placed the cover literal at raw offset 330847 when it starts at 330839. Neither could go red: evals/heldout/README.md counts SIX prior occasions where the verification instrument rather than the pipeline was at fault, and its remedy has always been a stricter rule for humans to follow, never an executable one. This case makes the rule executable for the three claim shapes the provenances actually use, and it covers all seven held-out cases, not only the two this PR added — 23 pre-existing occurrence-count claims across mrk-1995, spg-2019, intc-2025 and c-2025 are re-derived every run. WATCHED RED BEFORE THE FIX: at 353e8f1 the check reported exactly 2 failures, the intc-2025 offset mismatch and the c-2025 un-named regex, and 0 after. It reads fixture bytes only and imports nothing from src/sec10k, so it never invokes the extractor on a held-out filing and does not touch the isolation rule. PR #52 R11 — THE CHECK FAILED OPEN AND NOW FAILS CLOSED. As first written it returned green when it extracted nothing, so the coverage this provenance advertises could be reduced to zero with the gate still reading 123/123. Two one-line mutations were watched green before the fix: replacing mrk-1995's ASCII apostrophes with typographic ones (all four of its pins gone at once) and rewording `'Vasotec' 8x` to `'Vasotec' appears eight times`. Both now go RED against the `min_claims` floors above, which commit how many claims each file must yield and treat a vanished case file as a failure — the `evals/bench.check_docs` precedent, where a vacuous run exits 1 and its `_demo` asserts so. The patterns also accept typographic quotes now, closing that disarm route at the source rather than only at the floor. Claim inventory at this commit: c-2025 13 (8 counts, 3 raw offsets, 2 regex hit counts), intc-2025 8, spg-2019 5, mrk-1995 4 — cost-2022, csco-2016 and pgr-2023 state no byte-level claims in these shapes and are deliberately floorless rather than forced into the idiom. NOT PINNABLE, stated so it is not mistaken for coverage: intc-2025's SCAN offsets (571,466 / 567,879 / 232,331 / 328,627) are positions in a tag-strip rendering, not in the committed bytes, so verifying them would mean reimplementing the authoring scan inside the gate and pinning the instrument to itself. HOW THE RED WAS OBSERVED — CORRECTED UNDER PR #52 R14. The pre-fix reds recorded above (the 2 failures at 353e8f1, and the two fail-open mutations) were observed by calling the check function directly. This case has always declared `input.checks` and so has always been reachable from the gate — unlike its sibling `ledger-line-refs.json`, which was not — but a direct call proves nothing about reachability, so the claim is now made the only way it should be. RE-OBSERVED THROUGH THE RUNNER, `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant`: rewording `'Vasotec' 8x` to `'Vasotec' appears eight times` gives [FAIL] heldout-provenance-claims, invariant 60/61; `'Vasotec' 9x` gives [FAIL], 60/61; stripping every count shape from the file gives [FAIL], 60/61; the clean tree gives [PASS], 61/61. 2026-08-27 (D11, PR #58): the `intc-2025-heldout.json` floor of 8 pinned claims is REMOVED because that case was burned by the live exam and moved to `evals/adversarial/intc-2025-collapse-burned.json` with its fixture to `evals/fixtures/intc-2025/`. The check fails closed on a vanished file — it caught this move on the first run after it, which is the check doing its job — so the removal is recorded here rather than made silently. What is genuinely LOST: this check only scans `evals/heldout/`, so those 8 byte-level provenance pins are no longer enforced anywhere. The remaining floors cover 22 claims across the 3 surviving held-out cases that carry byte-level provenance. See the Burn entry in `evals/heldout/README.md` and the replacement debt row in `tasks/TODO.md`.
